B: Hi, hello. Can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Yeah, you're fine.
B: Great. I'm Rutendo.
A: Lee.
B: Nice to meet you, Lee. Erm, so where are you calling from?
A: Wakefield. You?
B: Coventry. Earlsdon, if you know it. Probably not.
A: Nah. Been through Coventry on the M6, that's about it.
B: That's most people, yeah. What do you do for work?
A: Sales rep. For a builders' merchants, timber, all that. I cover trade accounts, so site managers, small builders, round West Yorkshire and a bit into South Yorkshire. Basically I live in the car.
B: Oh, so you'd know all about materials and things. That's actually quite close to what I do, in a funny way.
A: Go on.
B: I'm an occupational therapist, for the council. So I do home assessments. Someone's come out of hospital, or they've got a disability, and I go round and work out what they need. A grab rail by the toilet, a stair lift, whether the kitchen needs changing, that sort of thing. So I'm always in people's bathrooms going, right, this wall's plasterboard, we can't put a rail on that.
A: Yeah, you can, you just need the right fixings. Or a backing board.
B: See, that's exactly the kind of thing the contractors tell me and I'm writing it down, you know?
A: It's not hard. People overcomplicate it. I fitted me own kitchen worktop. Bit wonky but it's still up.
B: Still up is the main thing, yeah. That's my whole job, really, still up and nobody falls over.
A: Fair enough.
B: What did you make of that puzzle at the start?
A: I mean, it were all right. Bit pointless. I just want to know when we get paid, if I'm honest.
B: Ha. That's honest, yeah. I quite liked the shape ones. Erm, is that your son in the photo behind you? In the uniform?
A: Yeah, Kieran. He's eleven. Just started secondary.
B: Oh, big change. How's he finding it?
A: All right, I think. He doesn't tell me owt. Comes in, says it's fine, goes on the PlayStation. It's just me and him, so. Me mum helps with the school runs when I'm out on the road. Don't know what I'd do without her, really.
B: That's a lot to juggle with all the driving.
A: You just get on with it. You got kids?
B: No, no kids. Just me. I keep telling myself I'm getting a cat next year. I've been saying it for about five years.
A: Get a cat, then.
B: That's very good advice, actually, thank you. Erm, what do you do when you're not working? Is that a rugby scarf?
A: Trinity. Wakefield Trinity, rugby league. I go to most home games. Five-a-side on a Wednesday if me mum'll have Kieran. That's me, really, that's about it.
B: I don't know rugby league at all, I'm sorry. I'm more of a galleries person. I go to the Herbert a lot, the gallery in Coventry, and the theatre.
A: Went to the Hepworth once. For a school thing of Kieran's.
B: Oh, the Hepworth! That's a beautiful building. What did you think?
A: It were all right. Bit much.
B: Bit much is fair. Some of it is a bit much, to be honest. Which bits did you
